doc.description:
Digital Photo Camera Triggering (using a UART link)
This module controls triggering of an attached external digital camera via UART commands.
This module fullfills 4 functions: 1) send shoot commands over UART 2) Besides triggering the shooting of images, the module also sends attitude and other relevant data. Typically an external linux camera or linux computer will receive the attitude and position data and add it to the photos. 3) The module will also parse the replies received over the UART. This contains status but can also contain sensor results, e.g. computer vision, to able to interact with the flightplan. 4) Finally, the module can also relay over telemetry all data it receives from the attached computer or camera using the PAYLOAD message. This can for instance be used to downlink thumbnails. 5) Targeted commands digital_cam_uart_shoot(id, report), digital_cam_uart_start(id), and digital_cam_uart_stop(id) address one camera (0=all, 1=CHDK, 2=AI cam, 3=LWIR, 4=EARcam, 5=Diplacam). These IDs are not masks. Regular DC_SHOOT uses digital_cam_uart_camera_mask: bit 0=CHDK, bit 1=AIcam, bit 2=LWIR, bit 3=EARcam, bit 4=Diplacam. Bits 5 through 7 address reserved future cameras; USHER reports them UNSUPPORTED until an actual backend exists. Examples: 0=none, 5=CHDK+LWIR, 10=AIcam+EARcam, 15=first four, 255=all eight slots. Define DIGITAL_CAM_UART_CAMERA_MASK for the startup mask (default: all eight slots). The obsolete DIGITAL_CAM_UART_CAMERA_ID define is rejected at build time. Flight plans and the GCS setting use uart_cam_ctrl_set_camera_mask(mask), which accepts integer masks 0 through 255 and retains the old mask on invalid input. uart_cam_ctrl_set_camera(id) selects one camera slot (IDs 1 through 8; 0=all). Selecting sends no command, does not reset autoshoot, and does not change numbering. A zero mask suppresses normal shots entirely. Each nonzero trigger sends one USHER_SHOOT_MASK frame with one photo number shared by all selected cameras. Build and deploy matching FC and MORA software; the session and point-result messages are a breaking protocol change and old peers are not compatible. Physical optical captures are serialized; they are not exposure-synchronized. Other modules can register a receive handler for USHER messages this module does not consume. A camera that reports a deduced geographic point needs no handler: the transport validates USHER_CAM_POINT_RESULT into digital_cam_uart_camera_point, and digital_cam_point applies it to a waypoint. digital_cam_uart_start(id) and digital_cam_uart_stop(id) open and close a camera session; a camera that accumulates evidence over time answers the stop with one point. Start invalidates the selected cameras' previous answers and allocates a nonzero session token. Stop echoes the same token; only one matching answer is accepted after stop. Replies from previous sessions or peers cannot satisfy the wait. Session commands contain camera_id and session_id (8 bytes); point replies contain camera_id, session_id, status and six signed fields (36 bytes). Deploy both peers. Stopping all cameras reserves the complete batch before emitting any frame and retains each camera's own token. A camera without a point backend returns INVALID.
Pose samples can be enabled unconditionally with DIGITAL_CAM_UART_POSE_STREAM=1 or leased by USHER clock probes. The stream emits USHER_POSE_SAMPLE from the existing 10 Hz periodic task; a camera session that relies on pose-driven evidence needs one of these mechanisms enabled. Unclocked frames use 105 UART bytes and require 158 free bytes. After a clock handshake, USHER_POSE_CLOCKED uses 113 bytes and requires 166 free bytes to leave space for one masked shot command. A full or smaller buffer skips the sample. The stream does not trigger a shot or alter the configured shot interval. The FC sends only requested shots and transport timing data. Flight plans select cameras and decide when to shoot; USHER owns capture processing. Timed, distance, circle and survey autoshoot evaluate a tick only when a complete ordinary shot frame fits; otherwise that tick is deferred. Reply consumers register by message ID so independent applications cannot replace one another. Unknown reply IDs are ignored. By default, every admitted FC trigger sends DC_SHOT telemetry once, showing one number on the GCS even for multiple cameras. DIGITAL_CAM_UART_SHOT_REPORT_MASK selects which camera bits permit that report (default: 255). Set it to 239 to silence Diplacam-only requests, 255 to report all, or 0 to report none. A mixed request reports once if any requested bit is enabled. Flight plans and the GCS shot report mask setting use uart_cam_ctrl_set_shot_report_mask(mask), which accepts only integer values 0 through 255. Invalid values leave the policy unchanged. The runtime policy survives peer reconnection and is independent of capture selection, autoshoot, session and point handling. Targeted digital_cam_uart_shoot(id, false) always suppresses the report; true permits it only when the reporting mask includes a requested camera. Every admitted trigger still advances shot numbering, including silent requests; a rejected trigger advances neither numbering nor reports. USHER returns one token/shot-number correlated terminal result per requested camera bit. FC arrays digital_cam_uart_camera_result_number[ID-1] and digital_cam_uart_camera_result_status[ID-1] expose results for flight plans; SAVED means original + required EXIF published, RECORDED is only an acoustic sample, FAILED/SUPERSEDED/UNSUPPORTED are not saved images. Missing feedback is unknown, not proof of failure. UART admission never proves capture. Generic camera controls use uart_cam_ctrl_command(mask, command, value), uart_cam_ctrl_zoom(mask, value) and uart_cam_ctrl_retract(mask). They return a nonzero ticket only after whole-frame admission; zero means not sent. Use call_once with assignment in flight plans, then read-only uart_cam_ctrl_command_pending(ticket) and uart_cam_ctrl_command_result(ticket). Check CAM_CONTROL_APPLIED explicitly; ending a wait is not success. The 70-second deadline becomes UNKNOWN, with no automatic replay. uart_cam_ctrl_control_ready() requires a fresh confirmed control session; uart_cam_ctrl_supports(mask, command) queries capabilities without sending. Result/value/evidence helpers use camera IDs 1..8, not masks. Controls use 188 bytes of additional fixed FC state and do not change photo numbers, capture selection, autoshoot or DC_SHOT reporting. Live CHDK supports optical zoom 0..255 and powered playback-mode retract. Playback evidence does not sense physical retraction; later capture or zoom can extend the lens. Other backends and keep-awake controls are unsupported. See Sensoraia docs/camera-control-proposal.md for examples and the contract. Updated USHER automatically probes the clock for live cameras. An accepted probe leases 10 Hz pose streaming for two seconds without activating survey mode; USHER --no-clock-align opts out. A clocked pose plus a reserved shot command needs 166 free bytes. No partial frame is emitted under backpressure. USHER --pose-log DIR stores optional schema-2 evidence; mapped poses also supply observation-time geotags independently of logging and survey profiles. Pose flags retain GPS-present in bit 0. Bit 1 marks GPS-held horizontal position, bit 2 validates GPS age, and bits 8 through 31 hold that age in ms. Physical ins_alt_float with its default GPS source advertises this evidence; NPS, other estimators and custom INS_ALT_GPS_ID overrides do not. USHER may advance only marked positions using NED velocity and at most 500 ms of GPS receipt age. Navigation state and original shot messages are unchanged. The payload sizes remain unchanged. Upgrade both peers to interpret the new flags. Receiver-internal latency and absolute target accuracy still require measurement; clock alignment alone does not establish either.
On sim and nps targets, this module owns its serial transport. It prefers DIGITAL_CAM_UART_LOCAL_DEVICE (/tmp/usher-sim) whenever local USHER is available and otherwise uses DIGITAL_CAM_UART_FALLBACK_DEVICE (/dev/ttyUSB0). It checks every 200 ms and switches at runtime; hardware targets require an explicit CAMERA_PORT configuration, for example UART2 for the Bebop USB serial device /dev/ttyUSB0, at 115200 baud. Simulation device settings do not select a hardware UART.
The linux program used to parse the UART command is given in the subdirectory.

define.name: SHOT_REPORT_MASK
define.description: Camera bits permitting DC_SHOT reports; default 255, 239 silences Diplacam-only triggers

makefile.raw: vpath usher_protocol.c $(SENSORAIA_SRC)/src vpath camera_control.c $(SENSORAIA_SRC)/src $(TARGET).CFLAGS += -I$(SENSORAIA_SRC)/src $(TARGET).srcs += usher_protocol.c camera_control.c
ifeq ($(strip $(CAMERA_PORT)),) $(error digital_cam_uart: configure CAMERA_PORT with the hardware UART, for example UART2 on Bebop) endif
